name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visual: Mine AI website/product DESIGNS (the look), taste-learn from Eitan's picks.

name: Easel
text: I’ll pull Eitan’s latest design picks from the shared drive (folder: `/design-references/eitan-picks/2024-q3/`), then extract the top 10 highest-rated visuals (by his notes) into a local `eitan-picks-2024-q3/` folder. Next, I’ll run a quick `ffmpeg` batch to generate 3-frame thumbnails for each (1280x720, 3s duration) and save them in `eitan-picks-2024-q3/thumbnails/`. After that, I’ll open the thumbnails in a grid layout in Affinity Designer to compare color palettes, typography, and spacing—then drop the grid as `eitan-picks-grid.afdesign` into `/mine-ai/designs/reference/`.

name: Squint
text: Squint: Hold on—why assume Eitan’s "notes" are a reliable proxy for quality? His picks could be biased by mood, client pressure, or even his *own* design blind spots. Where’s the inter-rater reliability? You’re treating his subjective ratings as gospel without testing them against an objective standard. And `ffmpeg` thumbnails? That’s a glorified file dump unless you’re also analyzing color palettes, contrast ratios, or layout patterns—metrics that actually define "the look." Show me the evidence that his top 10 align with *design* excellence, not just his whims.
